outcome: Satisfaction rate of blood glucose control
cohort: The study included a total of 1,092 patients with gestational diabetes mellitus from nine randomized controlled trials.
finding: Pharmaceutical care significantly improved various maternal and fetal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus, including reduced adverse drug events, improved medication compliance, better blood glucose control, and decreased incidence of complications like pregnancy-induced hypertension, macrosomia, and neonatal asphyxia.
mod_finding: Pharmaceutical care was associated with a lower rate of cesarean section compared to traditional medical care (RR=0.73, 95%CI (0.64-0.84)).
birth_weight: Macrosomia was an outcome measured, indicating birth weight was considered.
gest_age: Premature delivery was an outcome measured, indicating gestational age was considered.
